ExplanationParts.CorpusEarnedOpening: Here the headword is either the act of lighting incense or the counted incense inside the longer one-stick-of-incense phrase; those grammatical units must not be treated as one undifferentiated noun.
EvidenceBody: Monastic regulations use the headword as an instruction to light incense and report. Wuzhun Shifan’s record narrates going to the hall to light incense and bow; other records narrate lighting incense before a verse or dedication. Chijue Daochong says that his disciple Deyan lit incense to request the formal discourse. Counted one-stick constructions remain in the separate phrase entry, and a table-of-contents string is excluded.

DraftEvidence.ZenBend: Linji Yixuan in source work C077n1710 matters in offerings and time-marking; the phrase remains distinct from taking up or burning incense.
DraftEvidence.CounterexampleOrLimit: The stored evidence supports this bounded deployment, not one uniform intention, appraisal, or imported doctrine.

Senses.Explanation: A stick of incense is a countable offering and a public unit of dedication, not merely fragrance in general. In 古尊宿語錄, 臨濟慧照禪師餘錄 utters the stored headword-bearing clause; that exact turn anchors this sense, while the other stored cases test its range rather than being assigned wholesale to 臨濟慧照禪師餘錄.
